question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix such that $A^2 = 5A - 6I$, where $I$ is the $2\times 2$ identity matrix. If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$, verify the equation and hence find $A^{-1}$ using the equation. Explain your reasoning and computation in detail.
explanation:
First compute $A^2$.

$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & -4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $5A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 10 \\ -10 & -15 \end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $6I = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$.

Thus $5A - 6I = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 10 \\ -10 & -21 \end{bmatrix}$.

Using the matrix equation $A^2 - 5A + 6I = O$.

Rearranging gives $A(A - 5I) = -6I$.

Thus $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{6}(A - 5I)$.

Compute $A - 5I = \begin{bmatrix} -4 & 2 \\ -2 & -8 \end{bmatrix}$.

Therefore $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix} -4 & 2 \\ -2 & -8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} \end{bmatrix}$.

options.C: The equation is not verified and $A$ is not invertible.
options.D: For the given $A$, $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-4\\4&5\end{bmatrix}$ but $5A-6I=\begin{bmatrix}-1&10\\-10&-21\end{bmatrix}$, so the stated equation is not verified; the actual inverse is $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}$.
